rv.q: It is a credit to Metcalf’s gifts that maybe, just maybe, we understand a little bit better why Nora left and Hillary stayed.
Hillary and Clinton is cogent, snappy and perceptive about political and emotional realities.
She lets you know how much her character both knows and hates.
This is Hillary’s life as it was, is and apparently ever will be, even in an alternative universe.
Hillary and Clinton reminds us, if anyone dared forget, why she’s so exciting, with her great intelligence and great versatility and her surplus of fierce, nervous energy that barely seems contained.
Ultimately, it feels neither sufficiently contemplative nor revelatory, its ruefulness becoming merely a punishment.
Hnath’s depiction of her behavior crossed an ugly line, as Hillary blatantly offers up a lie to explain Bill’s arrival on the scene.
But all the moments don’t really add up.
Not even two of the brightest stage stars
The only thing wrong in this fictionalized visit to the 2008 primary is that playwright Hnath has brought nothing of substance to the table.
No matter how you feel about the Clintons you’ll likely find it a once-over-lightly disappointment.
The cast, needless to say, couldn't be better.
That’s an especially spectacular achievement here.
Metcalf elevates this production with devastating take-downs.
It’s a slim, impressionistic portrait.
This restrained play may not tell us anything new, but it imagines a moment of personal history sympathetically.
It has a downbeat and depressing aura and very little occurs.

Our humanity belongs in our politics as a reminder of our vulnerability, not as a target for sand in the gears that grind out thoughtful solutions when grounded in what is truly important: protecting the dignity of us all.
But for now, it's those previous opinions we hold that act as additional characters in this vibrant social commentary comedy about the job of getting elected.
Metcalf, on the stage throughout the entire production, never loses her cool, raises her voice, or fails to keep us wrapped in her easy natural presence.
Hillary and Clinton is the wistful, Thornton Wilder-tinged mediation on HRC that no one asked for.
